title: Rat learning experiments as evidence for morphic resonance
summary: Rupert Sheldrake tells of Rat learning experiments as evidence for morphic resonance, about an unknown time at San Francisco Bay Area, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: London, New York, San Francisco, Melbourne, Beijing

tellings.quote: now there's actual evidence from a long series of experience with rats that that actually happens

plain: A biologist and author named Rupert Sheldrake has an idea he calls morphic resonance: once some members of a species learn something, others of the same species elsewhere find it easier to learn, as if nature has a kind of memory. Speaking with podcast host Jesse Michels, he says a long series of experiments with rats, in cities from London to Melbourne to Beijing, gives actual evidence that this happens. If true, it would mean learning can spread between animals with no ordinary contact.
